sourceEvidence.label: Pulsai 3D API, persistence, provider, and roadmap source

assessment.summary: Identity, spend authorization, and artifact access need one tenant boundary before public multi-user launch.

nonNegotiables: Anonymous requests cannot spend platform provider credits.
Private designs and artifacts require an authorized owner or member.
Deterministic local CAD and BYOK remain available.
assumptions: No measured authentication latency budget was supplied.

opportunities.title: Centralize identity, spend, and artifact authorization
opportunities.summary: Move resource ownership and paid capability checks behind one request principal and policy boundary.
opportunities.diagnosis: Design ids, ambient provider credentials, and public artifact URLs currently act as authority in different parts of the stack.

evidence.claim: Projects and jobs are persisted as public and owned by anon.
Design endpoints do not evaluate an authenticated principal against resource ownership.
Legacy artifact upload made objects public.
Auth, quotas, billing, and sharing need a common product boundary rather than separate endpoint conventions.

desiredInvariants: Every durable resource has one owner and optional explicit members.
Every private read or write is authorized against the final resource identity.
Platform-paid operations require an authenticated entitlement and quota reservation.
Public sharing is explicit, read-only, revocable, and separate from ownership.
Private GCS objects are returned through short-lived or authorized delivery paths.

options.title: Tactical anonymous containment
options.summary: Disable platform spend and public objects while retaining bearer-like random design ids.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Random ids reduce guessing but do not authorize access.
Fail-closed spend gate blocks ambient paid credentials.
Objects are private but the proxy still lacks tenant identity.

tradeoffs.assessment: Stops anonymous platform spend and direct public bucket reads; ownership remains unresolved.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise each paid provider with configured platform keys and no BYOK; verify no network call.

tradeoffs.assessment: Boolean gates are local; artifact proxy adds a backend hop.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare GLB download latency and backend egress.

tradeoffs.assessment: Streaming proxy retains no full artifact buffer.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure RSS during a large G-code download.

tradeoffs.assessment: Private proxy depends on backend availability but provider failures are contained.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run artifact fetch and provider-denial integration tests.

tradeoffs.assessment: One env switch makes platform spend visible and auditable.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Alert on any production instance reporting spend enabled.

tradeoffs.assessment: Free CAD and BYOK remain compatible; legacy paid endpoints fail closed.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run free E2E and BYOK contract tests.

residualRisks: Anyone obtaining a design id can still read or mutate it.
No per-user quota or revocation exists.

workPackages: Default platform spend and public artifacts off.
Add denial and privacy regression tests.
acceptanceCriteria: Anonymous paid-provider requests cannot reach provider network calls.
migrationNotes: Explicitly enable only in a protected operator environment.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Revert the gates only in a private environment; never on the public API.

options.title: Required OIDC tenant boundary
options.summary: Verify a standard OIDC JWT once, authorize every resource centrally, reserve quota before paid work, and use explicit share grants.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Resources receive a stable owner subject.
Spend requires entitlement and atomic quota reservation.
Artifact delivery is authorized or short-lived.

tradeoffs.assessment: Removes identifier-as-authority and ambient paid capability from public requests.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run cross-tenant read/write/export/artifact and quota bypass tests.

tradeoffs.assessment: JWT verification and owner lookup add work to API calls; JWKS and policy results can be cached.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure p50/p95 API latency with cached and cold JWKS.

tradeoffs.assessment: Bounded JWKS and policy caches add small resident state.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure per-instance RSS under representative tenant count.

tradeoffs.assessment: Quota reservation and idempotency contain provider retries; identity provider availability becomes a dependency.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test JWKS cache behavior during identity-provider outage.

tradeoffs.assessment: Requires OIDC configuration, auth telemetry, rate-limit storage, and support workflows.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run key rotation, account deletion, and quota reset drills.

tradeoffs.assessment: Existing anon resources need quarantine, claim, or deletion; APIs gain principal requirements.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Dry-run ownership migration and verify rollback snapshots.

residualRisks: Compromised user tokens retain that user's authority until expiry/revocation.
Incorrect share-grant policy can still expose selected designs.

workPackages: Owner/member schema and centralized authorize helper.
Authorized artifact delivery and explicit share grants.
acceptanceCriteria: Cross-tenant access is denied for every design subresource.
No paid call starts without entitlement and quota reservation.
migrationNotes: Keep tactical spend and private-object gates throughout migration.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable new account creation, restore the pre-migration data snapshot, and keep platform spend disabled.

opportunities.recommendation: Keep anonymous containment as the immediate gate, then require the OIDC tenant boundary before external multi-user testing.

openQuestions: Which OIDC provider should be the first hosted default?
Should anonymous designs be ephemeral-only or disabled entirely?
Which globally consistent quota store fits the target hosting model?
